concerns.location: tasks.md:T070 / T067 / T072 vs plan.md:Project Structure
concerns.text: T070, T067, and T072 all name `data/results/threshold_ci.json` as the deliverable, but plan.md's Project Structure specifies `data/results/threshold_report.json`. An implementer cannot deterministically produce the 'right' file — the verifier failure that T070 exists to repair was plausibly caused by exactly this filename/schema disagreement. Pick one canonical filename and key set and reconcile across tasks and plan.

T070 requires output 'with the schema-defined columns (reduction_pct, error_rate, depth, ci_lower, ci_upper)' but the completed-contracts list names only workflow, execution_log, and analysis_results schemas — `contracts/tradeoff_curve.schema.yaml` (a plan Phase-1 deliverable) has no delivering task and is not listed as complete. T070's verification criterion references a schema that may not exist; either add a task producing the tradeoff-curve schema or inline the exact column/key specification in T070 so it is self-contained.

T072 is too coarse for one task: it bundles (a) an end-to-end re-run with pytest + schema validation, (b) writing `specs/001-policy-compression-tradeoff/results.md`, and (c) documenting the paper-stage handoff. Each has a distinct deliverable and verification path. Split so the atomizer/executor can verify them independently (e.g., T072a verification run, T072b results.md, T072c handoff note).

T067's verification is an assertion, but the report schema keys (`invalid_workflow_count`, `excluded_count`, `status`) don't capture HOW exclusion is proven — the script should specify the cross-reference mechanism (e.g., workflow IDs in tradeoff_curve.csv's underlying per-run data vs `is_valid=false` set). As written, an implementer could satisfy the keys without a meaningful check. One sentence naming the ID-level cross-reference would make it deterministic.
